  • Appendix C: Glossary and Term Index

This appendix collects the terms, instruction families, and symbols that appear more than once in this book. Each term gets one row, and "Where Covered" points to the section that defines it.

Sorting rule: all terms sit in one A–Z list by the English term, ignoring backticks, $, periods, %, and underscores, with terms that start with a digit placed before A. To look up a SASS instruction by its mnemonic, see Appendix B.

Term One-Sentence Explanation Where Covered
128-bit SASS instruction word On Volta and newer architectures (including Hopper), every SASS instruction is 16 B wide; based on public reverse-engineering analyses, it packs the opcode, register operands, and control-bit scoreboard wait masks and stall counts (an encoding NVIDIA does not document) Chapter 6, Section 5
1.87 ms lower bound 9.0 GB of fixed weights divided by 4.8 TB/s, not a timing measurement Primer 1, Section 4
A/A null-hypothesis control Runs the exact same code as both A and B through the same paired benchmark and uses the maximum difference as the winning threshold Chapter 7, Section 1; Chapter 10, Section 3
accept / reject draft tokens Accepts draft tokens before the first mismatch and replaces the mismatch position with the target model's prediction Primer 1, Section 7
activation The intermediate result just computed by the preceding stage; it does not exist until the preceding step finishes Primer 2, Section 3
.aligned suffix The PTX specification defines a thread group for each instruction, and all threads in that group must execute the exact same instruction or behavior is undefined (the warp for barrier.cluster, the entire warpgroup for wgmma and setmaxnreg, and the entire CTA for bar.sync) Appendix A, Section 2
all-gather Concatenates the slices from all 8 GPUs into the full output Primer 2, Section 2; Chapter 9, Section 1
all-reduce Sums the results from all 8 GPUs elementwise Primer 2, Section 2; Chapter 9, Section 1
arithmetic intensity III FLOPs performed per byte moved, in FLOP/B Primer 2, Section 4
async region and serialization hint Mix normal instructions into an async region and ptxas drains and waits after each instruction one by one Chapter 6, Section 6
asynchronous launch Once a command enters the queue, the CPU keeps running without waiting for the GPU to finish Primer 3, Section 2
ATOMG / REDG Global atomic with a return value; ignore the return value and it compiles to a fire-and-forget reduction Appendix B, Section 6
atomic add An indivisible read-modify-write addition that returns the old value Chapter 2, Section 6
attention Compares queries Q against keys K for similarity, then takes a weighted sum of values V Primer 1, Section 2
autoregressive generation Each new token comes from the tokens before it, so you can only generate tokens one by one Primer 1, Section 6
BBB (batch size), LLL (sequence length per request), T=B×LT = B \times LT=B×L (total tokens) Number of requests, number of new tokens per request, and total number of tokens Primer 2, Section 5
__ballot_sync warp-vote bucketing Computes prefix positions via warp voting Chapter 8, Section 6
bandwidth Bytes transferred per second; device memory bandwidth is measured in TB/s Primer 1, Section 4
bank conflict Lanes in the same warp access different words in the same shared-memory bank, splitting the access into multiple transactions Chapter 3, Section 7
base clock The lower rated clock frequency in the GPU specification; under default settings, NCU may pin the SM and memory clocks to this frequency (see Chapter 10, Section 1) Chapter 10, Section 1
BF16 (bfloat16) 16-bit floating point formed by the upper 16 bits of FP32 Primer 1, Section 1; Chapter 6, Section 1
BF16x2 (__nv_bfloat162) Packs two BF16 values side by side into one 32-bit register Chapter 5, Section 7; Chapter 6, Section 2
bitwise determinism (deterministic) Floating-point addition is not associative, so a non-deterministic reduction order may alter the least significant bits Chapter 2, Section 7
Blackwell (B200) Compilation target sm_100a, with ~8 TB/s bandwidth Appendix A, opening
block-scaled MMA Tensor Core instruction where both A and B are low-bitwidth floats, scaled per block before multiply-accumulate (one factor per 16 elements for 4-bit NVFP4, per 32 for FP8) Appendix A, Section 3
boundary kernel At the end of Stages 3 and 8, updates the residual and computes the normalization for the next input Chapter 9, Section 1
branch divergence When threads in the same warp take different branches, execution time equals the sum of both branches Chapter 4, Section 4
bucketing and grouped GEMM First groups tokens routed to the same expert together, then launches one grid per projection Chapter 8, Section 2
busiest GPU (straggler rank) The GPU whose local experts receive the most (token, expert) hit pairs in a layer (at T=1T = 1T=1, also the GPU that touches the most distinct local experts); this GPU sets the latency of the whole layer Primer 2, Section 1
bytes in flight Bytes whose read requests have gone out while the data has not yet returned to the SM Chapter 2, Section 3
C12 (12-bit lossless weight format) Retains the BF16 low byte, sign bit, and a 3-bit window offset, for 12 bits in total Chapter 6, Section 1
cache hit / cache miss A hit when the requested data is already in the cache level being checked (such as L1 or L2); a miss when it is not and must be fetched from the next level or HBM Chapter 2, Section 2
causal attention Each token attends only to itself and earlier tokens, never to later tokens Primer 1, Section 2
chunked prefill Splits a long prompt into chunks and runs them one after another (16,384 tokens per chunk in this book's examples) Primer 2, Section 5
clock cycle One tick of the SM clock; about 0.56 ns at 1.8 GHz Chapter 2, Section 2
coalesced access (coalescing) Addresses falling into the same sector merge into a single request Chapter 3, Section 2
commit group (commit_group / wait_group<N>) Waits until at most N committed groups remain incomplete before continuing Chapter 5, Section 5
completion flag Set after a subtask finishes writing to notify consumers waiting on it Chapter 8, Section 11
compute-sanitizer Checks intra-kernel data races and CTA barrier misuse, but cannot see cross-kernel races Chapter 10, Section 4
cooperative launch The driver guarantees that the whole grid is resident at one time; if the grid does not fit, the driver rejects the launch Chapter 2, Section 6
cp.async Asynchronous copy that moves data directly from global memory into SMEM without passing through registers Chapter 3, Section 3
CPU launch gap The command queue drains empty, leaving the GPU waiting for the CPU to issue the next command Chapter 1, Section 1
critical path The longest chain of dependency edges; single-layer latency equals the critical path plus CUDA graph replay overhead Chapter 9, Section 1
CTA barrier __syncthreads() Holds until all threads in the CTA arrive and makes prior writes visible across the whole CTA Primer 3, Section 4
cuBLAS / torch.mv The NVIDIA matrix library and the PyTorch baseline Chapter 4, Section 6
CUDA Core One FP32 lane of the FMA pipeline (32 per SMSP) Chapter 5, Section 1
CUDA event (inter-stream event) A marker recorded on one stream that another stream can wait on Chapter 9, Section 1
CUDA Graph A pre-recorded dependency graph of GPU commands that replays in a single launch at runtime Chapter 1, Section 2
CUDA graph replay overhead The latency of replaying a CUDA Graph containing only 1 empty kernel once Chapter 9, Section 1
CUDA stream A queue of GPU commands executed in enqueue order Primer 3, Section 2
cumulativity A release operation publishes both its own prior writes and writes from other threads that it has already observed Chapter 2, Section 6
CUPTI (CUDA Profiling Tools Interface) NVIDIA's profiling and tracing interface; this book uses its Activity API to record the start and end timestamps of every kernel in a graph replay without replaying kernels in isolation Chapter 10, Section 1
data race Two threads (in the same kernel or different kernels) access overlapping addresses with at least one write, no causality order between them, and not both morally strong (such as atomic operations) Chapter 9, Section 5
decode (token-by-token decoding) Each forward pass takes only the 1 token just produced, and the next token must wait for this pass to finish Primer 1, Section 6
dedicated release thread Each consumer performs only a CTA-scope release; a single dedicated thread then issues one GPU-scope release to notify other SMs Chapter 8, Section 11
dependent-instruction latency The number of clock cycles from when an instruction issues until a dependent instruction can use its result Chapter 5, Section 1
desc[URn] (uniform-register memory descriptor) A 64-bit memory descriptor held in a uniform register Appendix B, Section 1
device-wide memory barrier A gpu-scope memory barrier sequence (MEMBAR.ALL.GPU, etc.) that waits for this thread's prior writes to reach L2 and invalidates L1 on this SM Chapter 8, Section 11; Appendix B, Section 2
diagnostic tree (six-level) Timeline, full GPU, single SM, scheduler, pipelines, and SASS Chapter 10, Section 6
directed acyclic graph (DAG) Arrows mean "must wait for its result"; each layer has one main chain Primer 2, Section 3
disassembly Recovering SASS text from binary machine instructions Chapter 6, Section 5
drafting mechanism (draft model) A mechanism that guesses the next 7 candidate tokens first, such as a small draft model Primer 1, Section 7
drain latency The extra wait exposed from issuing the last wgmma until all results are written back to registers Chapter 5, Section 5
E2M1 / E4M3 Bit layouts for 4-bit floating point and 8-bit floating point (FP8) Chapter 6, Section 3
eager mode The CPU launches kernels one by one without recording a computation graph Chapter 9, Section 5
embedding table A table indexed by token ID to look up rows, of shape [202,048, 8,192] Primer 1, Section 1
EP8 (8-way expert parallelism) Assigns different experts to different GPUs, with 32 local experts per GPU Primer 2, Section 1
escaped weight (outlier) and side table Any weight whose exponent falls outside the window keeps an in-window placeholder code in the main table while its true value is logged in a side table, to be corrected either by adding the delta to the output or by patching registers Chapter 6, Section 1
even-odd ledger (ping-pong counter array) Two counter arrays that alternate by launch index; while one is in use, the other is zeroed Chapter 8, Section 12
F2F and F2FP Scalar floating-point conversion F2F executes on the SFU, whereas packed conversion F2FP does not occupy the SFU Chapter 8, Section 16
feed-forward network (FFN) Multiplies the input by the gate matrix and by the up-projection matrix, multiplies the two results elementwise, and then applies the down projection Primer 1, Section 2
fence.sc (sequentially consistent fence) Sequentially consistent fence you need when threads wait on each other's flags or when multiple flags must follow a single total order Appendix B, Section 6
fixed overhead Timing a single empty kernel with events takes about 4.6 µs, which covers launch, event recording, and running the empty kernel itself Primer 3, Section 5
fixed weights Dense weights that every token uses with no routing selection, plus lm_head; each GPU must read them on every forward pass (~9.0 GB for at most 8 tokens) Primer 1, Section 4
FLOP (floating-point operation) Floating-point operation count; one multiply-add counts as 2 FLOPs Primer 1, Section 4
FMA / ALU / SFU pipelines Execution pipelines with instruction issue intervals of 1, 2, and 8 cycles Chapter 5, Section 1
four hardware limits Four limits such as the register file pool and 4-warp warpgroup issue that software cannot change and can only work around Chapter 10, Section 10
FP8 (8-bit floating point) 8-bit floating point; E4M3 uses 1 sign bit, 4 exponent bits, and 3 mantissa bits Primer 1, Section 2; Chapter 6, Section 3
gemv (matrix-vector multiplication) Matrix-vector multiplication y=Wxy = Wxy=Wx — matrix multiplication at T=1T = 1T=1 Primer 2, Section 2
subtask table In the persistent wgmma kernel, each CTA builds the same subtask order in shared memory and dynamically claims subtasks via a global counter Chapter 8, Section 9
%globaltimer A predefined 64-bit global nanosecond timer register in PTX used for timestamp probes (cross-SM synchronization is not guaranteed by the specification) Chapter 10, Section 5
GQA (grouped-query attention) Divides the 16 query heads per GPU into 2 groups of 8, where each group shares 1 KV head (16 KV heads across the full layer) Primer 2, Section 1
grid barrier All CTAs increment the same L2 counter by 1 and wait until it reaches the total CTA count (waiting for all CTAs to arrive) Chapter 7, Section 12; Chapter 8, Section 6
grid truncation and tail loop Bounds the main grid's tile count at twice the per-GPU average hit-pair count (~T pairs), leaving any excess tiles to the tail loops inside the main kernels Chapter 8, Section 14
griddepcontrol.wait / griddepcontrol.launch_dependents The PDL wait and trigger calls; see Appendix B for SASS Chapter 8, Section 8
H200 An NVIDIA data-center GPU; this book examines a single H200 Preface, Section 1
handoff gap A successor kernel must wait for all CTAs of the preceding kernel to exit; Chapter 9 measures the time from when the preceding kernel's last CTA exits until the successor kernel's first wait returns Chapter 1, Section 1; Chapter 9, Section 6
happens-before Without PDL: a later command in the same stream sees all writes of an earlier command; with PDL, see "two visibility paths of PDL" in this table (Chapter 9, Section 5) Primer 3, Section 2
HBM (High Bandwidth Memory) Main GPU device memory; H200 has a nominal peak bandwidth of 4.8 TB/s Primer 1, Section 4
HGMMA The SASS mnemonic for BF16 / FP16 wgmma (QGMMA for FP8) Chapter 6, Section 5
hidden size 8,192 numbers represent each token; that is its width Primer 1, Section 1
hit pair (tok,slot,e)(tok, slot, e)(tok,slot,e) A (token, slot) pair routed to local expert eee on this GPU Chapter 8, Section 1
Hopper The GPU architecture of H200, with compilation target sm_90a Chapter 1, Section 4; Appendix A, opening
in-order issue / scoreboard Warps issue in program order; the scoreboard marks registers whose loads have not returned, and a warp stalls only when an instruction uses one of them Chapter 4, Section 2
issue slot 1 per SMSP per clock cycle; switching warps takes zero cycles Chapter 4, Section 1
K-halves When the tail-wave remainder does not exceed half a wave's capacity, splits each row across two half-row CTAs Chapter 2, Section 5
kernel A program launched once on the GPU and executed together by many threads Primer 3, Section 1
kernel fusion Merges adjacent kernels so intermediate results stay on-chip Chapter 1, Section 3
key-value head (KV head) Segments of K and V of width 64: 16 per layer, 2 per GPU Primer 1, Section 2
KV cache Stores already computed K and V in each layer for later tokens to read Primer 1, Section 2
L2 cache The 60 MiB level-2 cache shared across all 132 SMs Chapter 2, Section 2
L2 residency hint (cache policy) A policy attached to load instructions that controls eviction priority in L2 Chapter 2, Section 4
lane / SIMT The 32 lanes of a warp; each time the scheduler issues from the warp, it issues 1 instruction, and the active lanes sitting at that instruction execute it together (under Independent Thread Scheduling, each lane has its own program counter) Chapter 4, Section 4
__launch_bounds__ Tells the compiler the maximum threads per CTA and minimum CTAs per SM so it caps per-thread register usage Chapter 3, Section 1
lazy rescaling Reserves logarithmic headroom and rescales only when a warp vote triggers it Chapter 7, Section 9
ldmatrix (SASS LDSM) One warp loads 8 × 8 sub-matrices from SMEM into registers Chapter 7, Section 10
left-shift FMA offloading Moves left shifts onto the FMA pipeline to reduce ALU cycles Chapter 5, Section 1
Little's Law Bytes in flight equal bandwidth times round-trip latency, which tells you how many loads to keep in flight Chapter 2, Section 3
lm_head (vocabulary projection) The matrix that scores every candidate in the vocabulary; the 202,048-row vocabulary is evenly divisible by 8, so it is split across 8 GPUs at 25,256 rows per GPU without padding Primer 1, Section 3
local expert An expert stored on the local GPU; out of 256 experts per layer, each GPU stores 32 Primer 1, Section 2
logit softcap Multiplies logits by a fixed scale factor sss and compresses them into [−c, c][-c,\ c][−c, c] via c⋅tanh⁡(⋅/c)c\cdot\tanh(\cdot / c)c⋅tanh(⋅/c) to prevent individual logits from growing too large Primer 1, Section 3
logits Unnormalized FP32 candidate scores of shape R × 202,048 Primer 1, Section 3
lower bound (roofline floor) The fastest possible time for a stage: the maximum of bytes divided by bandwidth and FLOPs divided by compute throughput Primer 2, Section 4
matrix descriptor / SS and RS modes A 64-bit value describing an SMEM matrix; SS when operand A is in SMEM, RS when operand A is in registers Chapter 5, Section 3
mbarrier An 8-byte hardware object in SMEM that tracks pending thread arrivals and pending transaction bytes Chapter 3, Section 5
MeM_eMe​ (tokens routed to expert eee) The number of tokens routed to expert eee, used to partition hit pairs into two regimes Chapter 8, Section 1
megakernel Fuses an entire layer into a single large kernel Chapter 9, Section 6
memory fence Explicitly orders when reads and writes before and after the fence become visible; on the GPU you must insert it yourself Chapter 2, Section 6
memory ordering (relaxed / release / acquire) Three orderings that control when reads and writes become visible to other threads Chapter 2, Section 6
memory scope (scope) The visibility range where a release or acquire operation takes effect Chapter 2, Section 6
memory synchronization domain A label CUDA attaches to each launch; by default, all kernels belong to the same domain Chapter 9, Section 5
memory-bound (HBM-bound) / compute-bound (Tensor Core-bound) When III is below the ridge point, execution waits on HBM; when III is above it, execution waits on compute Primer 2, Section 4
merged launch Merges router and pooler, which read the same input, into a single kernel launch Chapter 9, Section 7
MIO (memory input/output instruction queue) The memory input/output instruction queue inside an SM for shared-memory instructions, special math functions (MUFU), and dynamic branches Chapter 10, Section 7
Mixture of Experts (MoE) Each layer has 256 experts, and each token uses only the 8 highest-scoring experts Primer 1, Section 2
mma.sync (m16n8k16) A Tensor Core instruction issued by a single warp Chapter 5, Section 3
multi-token GEMM g0 → g5 The evolution chain for T=8..256T = 8..256T=8..256, stacking mechanisms across five levels Chapter 6, Section 8
named barrier A hardware barrier numbered 0..15 that waits only for a specified number of threads Chapter 5, Section 7; Chapter 7, Section 7
noise band The threshold for judging whether a single change yields a real speedup: paired differences must have the same sign in every round and exceed the span of medians across several rounds of the same variant; see Chapter 10, Section 3 for the values and measurement methods per operator Chapter 4, Section 6; Chapter 6, Section 8; Chapter 10, Section 3
Nsight Compute (NCU) A kernel-level profiler that replays a kernel across multiple passes to collect hardware counters Chapter 10, Section 1
Nsight Systems A system-level profiler that plots CPU launches and GPU kernel start/end times on a single timeline Chapter 10, Section 6
NVFP4 (4-bit floating-point format) 4-bit floating point where every 16 weights share a 1-byte scale factor Primer 2, Section 1
occupancy The number of resident warps divided by the 64 warp slots per SM Chapter 3, Section 1
offline weight permutation Permutes weights offline in decoding order, reducing decoding instructions from 31 to 8 Chapter 6, Section 3
online softmax Tracks the running maximum, denominator, and accumulator in a single pass, rescaling when each new block arrives Chapter 7, Section 3
open-loop staggering Issues activation p and slot 0 weights first, while the remaining slots spin-wait a fixed delay on the nanosecond timer before issuing (500 ns at T=1T = 1T=1, 600 ns at T=8T = 8T=8, and 0 at T=16/32T = 16 / 32T=16/32 in the final version) Chapter 8, Section 7
operator One computation step in a model, such as a single matrix multiplication Preface, Section 6
padding row Blank rows padded into a tail tile to reach the full tile row count Chapter 8, Section 5
paged KV cache Stores KV in page slots at arbitrary positions, while a page table maps logical pages to physical page slots Chapter 7, Section 1
paired ABBA benchmarking (A, B, B, A) Alternates runs in the order A, B, B, A to cancel linear drift and takes the median across multiple paired differences Chapter 7, Section 1
parallel slice reduction / ticket number S CTAs each reduce 1/S of the rows, claim a ticket via atomic add, and wait until all S CTAs arrive Chapter 2, Section 7
partial sum The dot product of each segment split along K, summed together afterward Chapter 2, Section 5
PDL (Programmatic Dependent Launch) Decouples "successor can be dispatched" from "predecessor writes are visible" Chapter 1, Section 4
per-K-step three-stage times HHH / DDD / MMM (HBM read / decode / MMA) The three stages of HBM read, weight decode, and matrix multiply; when buffered, the longest stage dominates Chapter 6, Section 4
persistent kernel A grid that launches only one wave of CTAs, where each CTA stays resident and claims work items in a loop Chapter 3, Section 1
perturbation test (ablation test) Uses a runtime parameter switch to skip the code under test (keeping the machine code unchanged) and measures the upper bound via paired benchmarking Chapter 10, Section 8
pre-expert RMSNorm (pre_expert_norm) Applies RMSNorm to the 4,096-dimensional activation between Stage 5 and Stage 6 Chapter 9, Section 3
predicate Short conditions do not branch: the instruction carries a predicate, and lanes whose predicate is false do not write back Chapter 4, Section 4
prefill Processes the whole known prompt in parallel in one forward pass and keeps only the last row Primer 1, Section 5
PRMT (byte permute instruction) Selects bytes using 4 hexadecimal nibbles to assemble a new 32-bit word Chapter 6, Section 2
producer / consumer (warp specialization) Producer warps issue TMA transfers while consumer warps perform computation Chapter 3, Section 5
programmatic dependent edge Allows the successor to launch before the predecessor finishes and wait only at wait Chapter 9, Section 5
prologue / epilogue Setup before the main loop; elementwise computation after the main loop and before writeout Chapter 1, Section 3
proxy PTX label for memory-access methods: normal thread accesses use the generic proxy while TMA and wgmma use the async proxy, requiring fence.proxy.async across proxies Chapter 3, Section 3
PTX / ptxas / SASS Virtual instruction set; backend assembler; actual machine instructions executed by hardware Chapter 6, Section 2
RRR (number of rows to predict) Takes 1 row in prefill and decode; takes 8 rows in verify Primer 1, Section 3
read flush Reads a 512 MiB buffer once before timing so that L2 holds only clean lines Chapter 10, Section 2
reduction Combining many partial sums into one value, such as adding 128 partial sums together Primer 3, Section 4
reference bound The single-layer lower bound the task sets for each scenario (T=1T = 1T=1 sliding-window layer 40.0 µs, T=1T = 1T=1 full-attention layer 44.2 µs, T=8T = 8T=8 sliding-window / full-attention layer 62.3 / 66.4 µs); it is not a lower bound on the bytes any version actually reads Chapter 9, Section 1
register / shared memory / global memory Thread-private; on-chip shared within one CTA; in HBM shared across all CTAs Primer 3, Section 4
register spilling (spill) Values that do not fit in registers spill to local memory in device memory Chapter 3, Section 1
rematerialization and sinking The compiler recomputes values instead of keeping them in registers; loads are sunk past wait points Chapter 8, Section 8
request / batch (BBB) The number of requests batched together in one forward pass, denoted BBB Primer 2, Section 5
residual stream (stream) The shared 32-bit main state that every layer merges its output into Primer 1, Section 1
ridge point The crossover value of arithmetic intensity; 206 FLOP/B on H200 Primer 2, Section 4
ring buffer Divides SMEM into N slots reused in a ring to overlap data movement with computation Chapter 3, Section 4
RMSNorm (root mean square normalization) Divides a vector by the square root of the mean of its squared elements to stabilize numerical range Primer 1, Section 1
RoPE (rotary position embedding) Rotates each pair of elements by an angle determined by the token position Primer 2, Section 2
route-alignment kernel In prefill, sorts hit pairs by expert and pads each expert to an integer multiple of the tile height BMBMBM (64 or 128 rows) Chapter 8, Section 14
router / pooler / unpooler router scores the 256 experts; pooler projects 8,192 dimensions down to 4,096; unpooler projects expert outputs back to 8,192 dimensions (at T≤8T \le 8T≤8, each GPU computes 1/8 of the columns) Primer 2, Section 1
row fill ratio The fraction of the 64 rows that hold useful data Chapter 5, Section 4
row-stride padding Adds 1 extra word to the row stride so the same column in adjacent rows shifts by 1 bank Chapter 3, Section 7
rule of three Observing 0 errors in NNN runs shows only that the error rate is below 3/N3/N3/N (95%) Chapter 10, Section 4
sector 32 B, the minimum request unit for global loads; 4 sectors form one cache line Chapter 3, Section 2
setmaxnreg A warpgroup-wide hint to change the per-thread register cap: dec returns registers to the CTA pool and inc claims them from the pool (blocking if the pool runs short); called at kernel entry in this book Chapter 3, Section 6
severe numerical corruption An output result whose relative L2 error against a verified-correct output for the same input exceeds 0.01 Chapter 9, Section 5
side stream A second CUDA stream that lets kernels independent of the main chain run in parallel Chapter 9, Section 1
single layer / full model Single layer means one decoder layer on one GPU (µs); full model means all 62 layers (ms) Preface, Section 6; Chapter 9, Section 8
single tile / 16-token segment Experts with up to 8 tokens fit into a single mma.sync tile; experts with 9–16 tokens run as one 16-token segment to share a single weight read, while those with 17–32 tokens are divided into two segments Chapter 8, Section 6
skewed routing A routing distribution where tokens pile onto a small number of experts Chapter 8, Section 1
sliding-window layer / full-attention layer A sliding-window layer attends only to the most recent 2,048 positions; a full-attention layer attends to the entire history Primer 1, Section 2
SM (Streaming Multiprocessor) The compute unit that executes instructions; H200 has 132 SMs Primer 3, Section 1
SMSP (SM sub-partition) 4 per SM, each with its own warp scheduler Chapter 4, Section 1
softmax Turns a vector of logits into weights that sum to 1, where the denominator sums over all candidates Primer 2, Section 2
speculative verification break-even condition The average number of tokens produced per round must exceed the ratio of (verify + drafting) latency to a single decode latency Primer 1, Section 7
Speed Of Light (SOL) The percentage of peak bandwidth or peak compute throughput reported by NCU Chapter 10, Section 6
speedup upper bound How much latency drops when a perturbation test skips the code under test — the most time you can save Chapter 10, Section 8
spin-wait Repeatedly reads a flag until its condition holds; requires both CTAs to be co-resident Chapter 2, Section 6
Split-K Splits K into S segments so S CTAs jointly compute one output Chapter 2, Section 5
Split-KV / lse (log-sum-exp) / merge step Splits keys into S segments, records lse per segment, and merges them exactly Chapter 7, Section 3
stall sampling share The profiler samples warps at a fixed cycle interval; this is the share of non-issuing samples that a given stall reason accounts for Chapter 10, Section 7
st.async Writes directly to remote shared memory across CTAs and tracks byte completion via mbarrier Chapter 7, Section 12
stmatrix Writes 8 × 8 sub-matrices from warp registers into SMEM Chapter 5, Section 7
subnormal number Floating-point numbers whose exponent bits are all 0; they are evenly spaced and fill the smallest range Chapter 6, Section 3
swap-AB (swapping operands A and B) Computes yT=WxTy^T = W x^TyT=WxT by placing 64 rows of WWW as the left operand Chapter 5, Section 4
SwiGLU Passes gate ggg through silu and multiplies elementwise by up-projection uuu Primer 2, Section 2
SwiGLU scale folding Folds the scale factors into the exponent argument and denominator, reducing per-element instructions from 9 to 7 (and to 6 in the final tanh form) Chapter 8, Section 13
TTT (tokens per forward pass) The number of tokens processed concurrently in one forward pass; the token-ID array has shape [T][T][T] Primer 1, Section 1
tail duration (CTA exit skew) The time within the same kernel from when the median CTA exits until the last CTA exits Chapter 9, Section 6
tail wave The final batch of CTAs that does not fill a full wave, leaving most SM slots idle Chapter 2, Section 1
tcgen05.mma Fifth-generation Tensor Core instruction whose accumulator resides in TMEM Appendix A, Section 1
Tensor Core The dedicated on-chip compute unit for matrix multiply-accumulate Primer 2, Section 4
tensor scale / block scale One FP32 tensor scale per projection matrix (W13W_{13}W13​, W2W_2W2​) of each expert, and one E4M3 block scale per 16 weights Chapter 8, Section 1
tensor shape Notation that gives the tensor name and the length of each dimension, with the data type as a lower-right subscript Preface, Section 6
thread / grid A single execution thread; all CTAs in one kernel launch together form a grid Primer 3, Section 1
thread block (CTA) A group of threads that process a block of work together and run on a single SM Primer 3, Section 1
thread block cluster / GPC / DSMEM A group of co-resident CTAs; a cluster of adjacent SMs; cross-CTA shared-memory reads Chapter 7, Section 12
three-hop pointer chain Reading one KV page traverses three pointer hops through seq_lens, the page table, and the physical page index Chapter 7, Section 6
tile A small block of WWW staged in SMEM for repeated reads across the whole CTA Chapter 3, Section 3
.tile::gather4 A single TMA command takes 4 row indices and gathers them into one tile Appendix A, Section 4
timestamp probe In-kernel code that reads %globaltimer to record per-stage elapsed time Chapter 10, Section 5
TMA (Tensor Memory Accelerator) Hardware unit where a single thread initiates asynchronous bulk copies (on Hopper, tensor copies support rectangular tiles and im2col, plus 1D contiguous copies) Chapter 3, Section 3
TMA tile reduction (cp.reduce.async.bulk) TMA atomically adds an SMEM tile elementwise into the output in global memory (inferred to happen at L2; not determined) Chapter 5, Section 7
TMEM (Tensor Memory) Dedicated on-chip Tensor Memory separate from vector registers; 128 rows × 512 columns (256 KiB) per CTA in the PTX specification Appendix A, Section 1
token The basic unit processed by the model, never abbreviated to "word" in this book Preface, Section 6
Top-8 kernel Selects the top 8 out of 256 experts using scores plus router_bias, normalizes their unbiased scores into weights, and writes topk_ids and topk_weights Chapter 9, Section 1
TP8 (8-way tensor parallelism) Partitions the same matrix by head across 8 GPUs, with each GPU computing one slice Primer 2, Section 1
trigger call / wait call After the preceding kernel issues a trigger call, its successor can enter SMs early; the successor's wait call returns only after the preceding kernel finishes and its writes are visible Chapter 1, Section 4
two visibility paths of PDL Issuing fence.release.gpu before launch_dependents makes writes visible as soon as the successor launches; otherwise writes become visible only after wait returns Chapter 9, Section 5
uniform register (UR) A scalar register shared across all lanes of a warp Chapter 7, Section 7
verify (speculative decoding verification) Checks all 8 draft positions in one forward pass, with R = 8 Primer 1, Section 7
vocabulary The table that maps tokens to integer IDs, with 202,048 entries in total Primer 1, Section 1
warp A group of 32 consecutive threads that issue the same instruction together when they have not diverged (see Chapter 4, Section 4) Primer 3, Section 3; Chapter 3, Section 1
warp shuffle (__shfl_xor_sync) Directly reads a neighbor lane's register within the same warp Chapter 4, Section 5
warpgroup 4 consecutive warps whose first warp index is a multiple of 4, or 128 threads in total Chapter 3, Section 6
WARPGROUP.DEPBAR.LE Drain wait for wgmma: waits until at most N groups remain incomplete (for bare DEPBAR.LE, see Appendix B, Quick Reference 2, Item 31) Chapter 6, Section 6
wave The number of CTAs the whole GPU can keep resident at once; 2,112 in v1 Chapter 2, Section 1
weight Fixed parameters in the model; every inference reads the same copy Preface, Section 1
wgmma (m64nNk16; k32 for FP8) Must be issued collectively by an entire warpgroup, with row height 64 Chapter 5, Section 3
write-after-read hazard (WAR) Marking a slot empty before its data enters registers lets the next TMA round overwrite it silently without raising an error Chapter 3, Section 5
XOR swizzle Permutes column indices by XOR to stagger shared-memory banks without extra space overhead Chapter 3, Section 7
zero-column shortcut In single-GPU benchmarks, the 7,168 columns owned by the other 7 GPUs are identically 0, so Stage 3 precomputes the sum of squares Chapter 9, Section 2
